source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

source4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_4.csv", index_col=0)
source5 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_5.csv", index_col=0)

source7 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_7.csv", index_col=0)
source8 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_8.csv", index_col=0)
source9 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/training_9.csv", index_col=0)

# UNION all source tables with the same schema (the 4 tables with many columns including CANCELED, ROW_WID, etc.)

# JOIN union_0 with all other aspect tables on ROW_WID

            .merge(source1, on="ROW_WID", how="inner") \
            .merge(source3, on="ROW_WID", how="inner") \
            .merge(source4, on="ROW_WID", how="inner") \
            .merge(source7, on="ROW_WID", how="inner") \
            .merge(source8, on="ROW_WID", how="inner")

# The target schema is only COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM, so we aggregate by summing COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM
# No group by columns because target has no keys and only one column
result = pd.DataFrame()
result["COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM"] = df["COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM"].sum()

# The sum returns a scalar, convert to DataFrame with one row
result = pd.DataFrame({"COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM": [result["COLLECTION_EVENTS_NUM"]]})

result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_29/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
